questions.question: Which recall campaigns are flagged as an over-the-air update in the recall records?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r WHERE overTheAirUpdate = true
questions.note: None: the overTheAirUpdate flag is false on all 29 recalls (as are parkIt and parkOutSide). The tempting answer lists the recalls whose remedy is a software update or reprogramming (15V406000, 15V436000, 16V725000, 16V244000), but those are done by dealers, and the flag says so.

questions.question: According to the remedy of recall 16V074000, were replacement parts already available when owners were mailed the interim notification?

expected.text: No. Parts were only expected to be available in the summer of 2016; owners were to be mailed a second notice when parts became available.

chunks.quote: Parts are expected to be available in the Summer of 2016.  Owners were mailed an interim notification beginning March 31, 2016, and will be mailed a second notice when parts are available.

questions.note: The interim notification went out from March 31, 2016, while the remedy says parts are only expected in the summer of 2016 and promises a second notice when they are available: an expectation, not availability. A reader that takes 'dealers will inspect and replace the piston assemblies' or 'Parts are expected to be available' as parts being on hand answers yes. H19 asks what dealers do under this recall and HE07 counts its interim notification; neither asks about the parts.

questions.question: On which floor of the parking structure did the vehicle in complaint 11010220 hit the concrete wall?

chunks.quote: HITTING THE CONCRETE WALL ON THE 6TH FLOOR OF THE STRUCTURE.

questions.note: The owner pumped the brake pedal twice before hitting the concrete wall on the 6th floor of the structure. The other numbers in the complaint (twice on the pedal, this Friday morning) are not floors.

questions.question: Which complaint was filed the largest number of days after the incident it reports?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints ORDER BY date_diff('day', strptime(dateOfIncident, '%m/%d/%Y'), strptime(dateComplaintFiled, '%m/%d/%Y')) DESC LIMIT 1
questions.note: 11209676 (2019 Toyota RAV4, will not accelerate) reports an incident on 12/20/2018 and was filed 05/24/2019, 155 days later. The runner-up is 11229137 (incident 03/01/2019, filed 07/03/2019, 124 days); the next, 11180230, waited 35 days. Dates are month/day/year.
